title: pastLessons(): what went wrong in a project's recent runs
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24 (imports end in .ts, erasable syntax only, no packages). Read src/types.ts (RunState: id, project.name, request, status, createdAt, tasks; Task: id, title, status 'pending'|'running'|'accepted'|'failed'|'skipped', attempts: Attempt[], critique?) and test/pick.ts (test style; builds partial RunState with `as unknown as RunState`).
1. Create src/lessons.ts with `export function pastLessons(runs: { s: RunState; report: string }[], project: string, currentId: string, maxRuns = 5, max = 15): string[]`. Keep runs whose s.project.name === project and s.id !== currentId, newest first by createdAt, take maxRuns. Per run, emit lines prefixed with `<run id>: `:
 - each task with status failed or skipped: `task <id> (<title>) <status> after <attempts.length> attempt(s)` plus `: <first line of critique, max 200 chars>` when critique is set;
 - each accepted task with attempts.length > 1: `task <id> (<title>) needed <n> attempts` plus the critique part the same way;
 - the lines under a `## Follow-ups` heading in report (until the next `## ` heading), each starting with `- `, without the `- `, max 200 chars each.
 Return at most max lines in that order.
2. Create test/lessons.ts covering: other project and current run ignored; newest run first; failed, retried-then-accepted and follow-up lines; max cap. Print `lessons PASS`.
3. package.json: append ` && node test/lessons.ts` to the "test" script.
Change nothing else.

title: Senior plans with lessons from the project's recent runs

checks.name: wired
checks.cmd: grep -q 'pastLessons' src/nodes/senior.ts && grep -q 'LESSONS FROM RECENT RUNS' src/prompts.ts

brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24 (imports end in .ts). src/lessons.ts exports `pastLessons(runs: { s: RunState; report: string }[], project: string, currentId: string): string[]`. Read planPrompt in src/prompts.ts (signature `planPrompt(s, snapshot, agents, terse)`, `snapshot,` sits in its returned array) and the senior.plan node in src/nodes/senior.ts.
1. src/prompts.ts: add a fifth parameter `lessons: string[] = []` to planPrompt and, right after `snapshot,` in planPrompt's array (not the one in understandPrompt), add: `lessons.length ? `LESSONS FROM RECENT RUNS OF THIS PROJECT (failures, retries, open follow-ups; plan around them, and turn a follow-up into a task only if the request needs it):
${lessons.map((l) => `- ${l}`).join("
")}` : ""`.
2. src/nodes/senior.ts senior.plan node: build `const runs = engine.vault.runs().map((r) => { const f = path.join(engine.vault.runDir(r.id), "report.md"); return { s: r, report: fs.existsSync(f) ? fs.readFileSync(f, "utf8") : "" }; });` and pass `pastLessons(runs, s.project.name, s.id)` as planPrompt's fifth argument. Import pastLessons from "../lessons.ts" and fs/path from node: if missing.
Change nothing else.

title: Engine git calls ignore a leaked GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Found in three real runs: agent shells with isolateGit export GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, and when they leak into the engine's environment every engine git step and npm test break. Read `git` in src/util.ts (spawnSync("git", args, { cwd, encoding, maxBuffer })).
1. In src/util.ts `git()`: pass `env` = a copy of process.env without GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE, so the engine's git always works on `cwd`. Add a one-line comment saying why. Do not change shell().
2. At the end of test/pick.ts (before `pick PASS`): create a temp dir, run `git(tmp, "init", "-q")`, set process.env.GIT_DIR = "/nonexistent", assert `git(tmp, "rev-parse", "--git-dir").ok` is true, then delete process.env.GIT_DIR. Import git from ../src/util.ts and fs/os/path as needed.
Change nothing else.
